text: Bangime is a language isolate spoken by 3,500 ethnic Dogon in seven villages in southern Mali, who call themselves the bàŋɡá–ndɛ. From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia. Language isolate of southeastern Mali. Not to be confused with the Bangi language of central Africa.

title: Bangime | Ethnologue Free
text: Bangime is a stable indigenous language of Mali. It is an isolate that is not known to be related to any other language. The language is used as a first language by all in the ethnic community.

title: Bangime: Secret Language, Language Isolate
text: Bangime is undoubtedly a language isolate, but it is not an insular language; we expect to see clear effects of contact with its neighbors. The most likely impact is from the Dogon languages, yet questions remain about when and which varieties left their mark.
